entries.title: Isaiah 47:1
segments:
O virgin daughter of Babylon; Babylon herself personified as a female. 
 
  No throne; that is, to thee. 
 
vv 1-5. 
 
No present degree of power, wealth, or splendor, can protect wicked and persecuting nations from the wrath of God.  He has pledged himself to humble every oppressor of his people, and for the fulfilment of his word all the resources of heaven and earth are at his disposal.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:2
segments:
Take the millstones; grinding, in the East, is a menial office. The mistress of nations must now take the place of a servant. 
 
  Uncover thy locks; remove thy veil; another sign of degradation. 
 
  Make bare the leg--pass over the rivers; she is represented as fording streams in the manner of a woman of the lowest condition.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:3
segments: Will not meet thee as a man; not as a frail man, but as the omnipotent God.  But some prefer to render, "I will meet no man;" that is, no one who can offer me any resistance.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:6
segments: It is no excuse to wicked men, that God employs them as the instruments of executing his purposes.  They will be judged according to the spirit and intention of their deeds, not according to the use which God's overruling wisdom makes of them.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:7
segments:
The latter end of it; of thy pride, luxury, and cruelty; that is, the disgrace to which they would bring thee. 
 
vv 7-9. 
 
A proud, self-sufficient, and contemptuous spirit is the harbinger of ruin to nations not less than to individuals.  When a nation thinks itself most secure from danger, it is often nearest to destruction.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:10
segments:
vv 10-15. 
 
When a nation has cast off the fear of God, and trampled under foot his holy law, no device of human wisdom can save it from speedy and utter ruin.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:11
segments:
From whence it riseth; or, "its morning."  It shall be a night of calamity, without any morning of prosperity. 
 
  Shalt not know; suddenly, and without notice beforehand.  Compare

entries.title: Isaiah 47:13
segments: Monthly prognosticators; those who pretend to foretell events from the changes of the moon.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:14
segments: Not be a coal--nor fire; the consumption shall be so complete that nothing shall be left.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:15
segments: Thy merchants; the merchants whose trade had enriched Babylon. Compare
